newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity lower with cool temps, demand.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity lower with cool temps, demand.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mostly lower with mild temperatures through much of the West and limited demand, industry sources said.
"Generally there are mild temperatures across the Southwest and cooler temperatures in the Northwest, and it's a shoulder month so demand is lower," said one futures broker.
October California Oregon Border (COB) ended down 13 cents at $15.37 after trade as high as $15.55 per megawatt hour (MWh), while November settled 10 cents lower at $16.30 after trading at $16.40.
Remaining COB deferreds were steady to 10 cents lower.
October Palo Verde (PV) closed the day down 32 cents at $15.73 after trading as low as $15.70, while November settled down 15 cents at $14.90.
Remaining COB deferreds were steady without having traded.
NYMEX said an estimated 361 COB contracts and 50 PV contracts traded Wednesday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
